guide: This is a repeatable way to turn a finished app into a short outreach message to your own contacts, so people can try it and give feedback. You need an app with a live link, a demo account, and your phone contacts or WhatsApp.
1. Put the app on a public link, for example by deploying it with Vercel.
1. Create a demo account in the app so a stranger can look around without signing up.
1. Write a two-sentence message: what the app is, and one clear thing you want (a sign-up or some feedback).
1. Ask ChatGPT or Claude to give you three versions of the message in your own voice, then pick the one that sounds like you.
1. Export your contacts into a Google Sheet and mark who the message suits, such as friends, former colleagues or people in your target audience.
1. Send each message in WhatsApp yourself, one person at a time, with their name at the top.
1. Log who replied and what they said in the same Google Sheet, and fix whatever they flag in the app.
1. Send a short thank-you to everyone who replied, then repeat with the next group.
Watch out: send every message by hand to people who know you; bulk-sending to a list breaks WhatsApp's rules and can get your number banned.

```
You are helping me ask my own contacts to try an app I have built. The app is <app name>, it does <one-line description>, and the link is <app URL>. There is a demo account: <demo login details, or "none yet">. My audience is <who the app is for>. I have my contacts in <Google Sheet / phone contacts / WhatsApp>.
Please do the following:
1. Write three short WhatsApp messages (under 50 words each) in a warm, direct, non-salesy tone. Each should say what the app is, give the link, and make one clear ask: <sign up / try the demo / reply with feedback>.
2. Suggest a simple Google Sheet layout with columns for name, group, message sent, replied, feedback and next step.
3. Draft a short thank-you reply and a follow-up for people who do not answer after a week.
4. Give me a checklist for sending manually, one person at a time, with no bulk-sending tools.
Use British spelling. Do not use hype or emoji. Return the messages, the sheet columns and the checklist as separate sections.
```
